subject.title: [Bug]: iOS app fails to connect over Tailscale CGNAT (100.x.x.x) — wss:// required but WebSocket upgrade silently dropped

question: What security policy should the iOS app use for Tailscale Gateway connections: require WSS/Tailscale Serve/MagicDNS only, allow an explicit raw Tailnet CGNAT plaintext exception, or defer raw Tailnet support and improve diagnostics/docs?
rationale: The current code and docs deliberately fail closed for Tailnet CGNAT plaintext, while the reported user path needs either a secure WSS route that actually works or a maintainer-approved exception to that boundary.

options.title: Secure Tailnet WSS path
options.body: Keep raw CGNAT plaintext rejected and make the iOS Tailscale Serve/MagicDNS TLS trust flow reliable, visible, and documented.

options.title: Explicit raw Tailnet exception
options.body: Allow `100.64.0.0/10` or `.ts.net` plaintext only behind a clearly named security policy and focused tests/docs.

options.title: Diagnostics-only for now
options.body: Keep current fail-closed behavior and improve iOS errors/docs so users know to use LAN or a configured WSS route.

recommendation.title: Secure Tailnet WSS path
recommendation.body: Keep raw CGNAT plaintext rejected and make the iOS Tailscale Serve/MagicDNS TLS trust flow reliable, visible, and documented.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work on Tailnet route advertisement and iOS setup-code probing makes this the best available routing owner for the policy choice.
